x.hook: Pooled margin models blow up your capital. Here is the fix.
x.copy:

We built Vanna around isolated SmartAccount sandboxes on Soroban. Each account runs separate state while routing 10x leverage across Blend b-tokens and Aquarius LPs at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas.

Liquidations trigger strictly at a 1.10x Health Factor floor, monitored at ~320ms Mercury indexer latency without pool contamination. Test it: test.stellar.vanna.finance

linkedin.hook: Why pooled risk models fail institutional DeFi credit underwriting.
linkedin.copy:
Risk managers at institutional desks avoid multi-protocol composability because shared collateral pools inherit worst-case counterparty drag. If a cross-margin protocol commingles assets, a cascading bad-debt event in an obscure yield strategy can impair an entire liquidity pool. On Stellar Soroban, where credit connectivity between Blend and Aquarius is currently missing, bridging this gap requires a structural firewall rather than higher reserve factors.

The architecture solves this through isolated SmartAccount sandboxes. Instead of routing leverage through a central escrow pool, every operator provisions a dedicated contract instance on Soroban. Debt from Blend b-tokens, automated market maker exposure on Aquarius, and trades through Soroswap remain compartmentalized within that specific address space. A liquidation event executes against that single contract at a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor, completely insulating external protocol liquidity.

Deterministic execution is the prerequisite for institutional balance sheets. Leveraging Soroban native execution, state transitions settle at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas while ~320ms Mercury indexer latency delivers predictable liquidation telemetry before bad debt accrues. Risk desks can evaluate the sandbox implementation directly at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: Why we abandoned shared liquidity pools for isolated Soroban SmartAccounts on Vanna
reddit.copy:
Composability between Blend (b-tokens), Aquarius (LP shares), and Soroswap currently does not exist natively on Stellar. If you want to run leveraged yield strategies across these primitives, you are forced to manage manual loops off-chain or accept pooled cross-margin protocols where another user's bad debt impairs your principal.

We took a different approach when architecting Vanna. Every user deploys an isolated SmartAccount instance on Soroban. This contract acts as an on-chain sub-account that borrows against collateral and executes positions directly across external protocols. Up to 10x leverage is supported, but the critical factor is containment. Debt obligations, LP tokens, and swap paths stay inside your specific sandbox contract.

The risk model operates under strict constraints. We maintain a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor where liquidations trigger deterministically before solvency degrades. Network overhead settles at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per state modification, and our Mercury indexer processes liquidation telemetry at ~320ms latency. Because positions are boxed in individual contracts, counterparty contagion is mathematically isolated. A sharp drop in an Aquarius AMM pool affects only the single account holding that position, leaving external lending pools intact.

You can inspect the contracts and spin up a test instance right now. Point your wallet to test.stellar.vanna.finance, mint mock testnet collateral, and deploy a SmartAccount sandbox. You can open a Blend b-token borrow, route through Soroswap, and LP on Aquarius in an atomic execution path.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol. We are actively stress-testing liquidation edge cases on testnet and welcome technical teardowns or audit feedback.
